images.title: The biggest and the smallest by one swap
images.purpose: Show 62,815 and the two numbers made from it by one swap: the biggest, 82,615, and the smallest, 12,865.
images.composition: One number train at the top centre and two arrows down to two trains side by side, the biggest on the left and the smallest on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Each train, left to right: 1 small flat blue #0072B2 engine (about 100 px wide, no text), then 5 square coaches about 90 by 90 px joined by short couplers, each coach with 2 round wheels and one digit in bold numerals (60 px). Above each train its number in bold dark numerals (56 px), under each coach a small place letter in dark text (30 px): TTh, Th, H, T, O. Top train, centred horizontally in the upper part: number 62,815, digits 6, 2, 8, 1, 5, all 5 coaches blue with white numerals. From under the top train 2 thick amber #E69F00 arrows leave, one slanting down to the left and one slanting down to the right. The left arrow carries the label biggest: swap 6 and 8, the right arrow the label smallest: swap 6 and 1 (40 px, dark). Bottom left train: number 82,615, digits 8, 2, 6, 1, 5; coaches 1 and 3 are reddish purple #CC79A7 with dark numerals (the two that moved), coaches 2, 4 and 5 are blue with white numerals. Bottom right train: number 12,865, digits 1, 2, 8, 6, 5; coaches 1 and 4 are reddish purple with dark numerals, coaches 2, 3 and 5 are blue with white numerals. The two bottom trains are about 100 px apart and each sits under its arrow.

images.takeaway: To make the biggest number bring the biggest digit to the front, and to make the smallest bring the smallest digit to the front.
images.description: A number train 62,815 with two arrows leading to the train 82,615, marked biggest: swap 6 and 8, and the train 12,865, marked smallest: swap 6 and 1.
images.context: Concept image for The biggest and the smallest by one swap. It shows before and after rows of digit coaches side by side and uses the video's own example, 62,815. The digit swap questions of your maths book use other numbers.
images.teaching_notes: The leftmost place has the most value, so look at it first. The coloured coaches are the two digits that moved. Never bring a 0 to the front.

image_decisions.why: Before and after trains side by side show how one swap gives the biggest and the smallest number.
